Phrasal verbs · B1

From team player
to gym girl.

Sport, people and everyday decisions. Learn eight phrasal verbs and use them to talk about real-life situations.

60-minute individual lesson · 8 target expressions

01 · Warm-up

Meet the squad

Turn over the cards to discover four different people. Choose two and compare their interests, personalities and routines.

Speak
Which character would you get on with best?

Choose one and explain your choice. Then compare two characters.

02 · Diagnostic task

Match the meaning

Match each phrasal verb to its meaning. Try it from memory before studying the definitions.

Matching
1. admire and respect someone
2. have a friendly relationship with someone
3. feel accepted as part of a group
4. accept something unpleasant
5. be as good as expected
6. reach the same level as someone / do what you missed

Check your matching to unlock the vocabulary explanations.

04 · Teach & notice

Eight phrasal verbs

Now check the meanings, notice the patterns and study the examples.

Vocabulary
01

look up to

admire and respect someone

Layla looks up to her former coach.

02

get on with

have a friendly relationship with someone

Ilya gets on with most of his teammates.

03

fit in with

feel accepted as part of a group

Julia wants to fit in with the new group.

04

put up with

accept something unpleasant

Peter can't put up with unreliable training plans.

05

live up to

be as good as expected

The gym didn't live up to the online reviews.

06

catch up with

reach the same level as someone; do what you missed

Peter needs to catch up with his training.

07

make up for

compensate for something

Layla trained on Sunday to make up for a missed session.

08

sign up for

register to take part in something

Julia signed up for a beginner's class.

Three-part phrasal verbs

Some expressions contain a verb and two particles. Keep the three parts together: look up to someone, get on with someone, put up with something.

Compare: make up = invent; make up for = compensate for something.

05 · Controlled practice

Choose the phrasal verb

Read the whole situation. Choose the expression that best completes each sentence. Focus on meaning, not just familiar words.

Meaning in context
PHRASAL VERB BOXQuick reference · Use these expressions in the task
look up toadmire
get on withhave a good relationship
fit in withfeel accepted
put up withtolerate
live up tomeet expectations
catch up withreach the same level
make up forcompensate
sign up forregister
1. Layla still respects her old basketball coach. She really ______ him.
2. Julia and the other fans have similar interests and enjoy spending time together. She ______ them.
3. Ilya is the newest player in the club. He wants the other players to accept him as part of the group. He wants to ______ them.
4. Peter's gym is always overcrowded, but he continues training there. He ______ the crowds.
5. The gym looked amazing online, but the equipment was old and the changing rooms were dirty. It didn't ______ Peter's expectations.
6. Layla missed three basketball practices because of exams. Now she needs to ______ the team.
7. Julia couldn't attend the weekend class, so she booked an extra session to ______ the missed workout.
8. Peter wants to try a beginners' climbing course, so he decides to ______ it.
Read each sentence again and explain why the chosen expression fits the situation.
06 · Controlled practice

Spot and fix the mistake

Each sentence contains one incorrect phrasal verb. Rewrite only the phrasal verb so that the sentence makes sense. Keep the correct verb form.

Error correction
PHRASAL VERB BOXQuick reference · Use these expressions in the task
look up toadmire
get on withhave a good relationship
fit in withfeel accepted
put up withtolerate
live up tomeet expectations
catch up withreach the same level
make up forcompensate
sign up forregister
1. Layla really gets on with her former coach. She respects him a lot.
2. Julia wants to put up with the other members of the new group and feel accepted.
3. Ilya can't catch up with the constant noise in the gym. It really annoys him.
4. The new training programme didn't make up for Peter's expectations.
5. After missing a week of classes, Julia needs to sign up for the group and learn what she missed.
6. Layla trained on Sunday to live up to the session she had missed on Friday.
After correcting each sentence, say what clue in the context helped you choose the phrasal verb.

Free practice · Task 2

The advice column

Choose one person and respond to their problem as a friend or a coach. Give practical advice and explain your reasons.

Layla misses playing basketball but is not sure whether she should return to a team.
There is no single correct answer. Check that your advice is relevant, supported with reasons and uses the phrasal verbs accurately.
